what_its_for: Cefdinir is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including ear infections, sinus infections, throat infections (strep throat), skin infections, and some types of pneumonia. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It will NOT work for viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take cefdinir exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If the liquid (suspension) form is prescribed, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with a dosing spoon or oral syringe — never use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow capsules whole with a full glass of water. Take every dose at evenly spaced times and finish ALL of your medicine, even if you start feeling better early. Stopping too soon can allow bacteria to grow back and become harder to treat.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, and the type of infection being treated. Common doses are: Adults and teenagers — 300 mg twice a day OR 600 mg once a day. Children — usually 7 mg per kg (about 3 mg per pound) of body weight twice a day OR 14 mg per kg once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Treatment usually lasts 5 to 10 days depending on the infection.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Capsules: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from moisture and heat. Liquid suspension: Store in the refrigerator or at room temperature — check your label for instructions. Throw away any unused liquid after 10 days. Keep all forms out of reach of children. Do not flush medications down the toilet unless the label says to do so.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (like Maalox or Mylanta) or iron supplements within 2 hours before or after taking cefdinir, because they can prevent your body from absorbing the medicine properly. Do not take more than your prescribed dose. Avoid drinking alcohol in excess as it may worsen certain side effects. Do not share this medicine with others, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a severe skin rash, hives, or blistering skin; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing (signs of a serious allergic reaction); severe or watery diarrhea (which could be a serious gut infection called C. diff); seizures; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or dark urine. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not start improving after a few days, or if they get worse at any point during treatment. Note: Cefdinir can turn your stools a reddish-brown color — this is harmless and not a reason to stop taking the medicine.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting cefdinir. However, it is very important to finish your entire course of treatment even if you feel completely well before it is done. If you do not notice any improvement after 3 days, or if you feel worse at any time, call your doctor.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor may need to lower your dose. Always tell your doctor about any kidney problems before starting this medicine. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing this medicine. Children: Cefdinir is safe for children 6 months of age and older when dosed correctly by weight. The liquid form is usually used for young children. Elderly patients: Older adults with reduced kidney function may need a lower dose. Your doctor will adjust as needed.
